title: Yarrow toner infusion for oily skin
subtitle: An astringent skin toner for oily or congested skin
excerpt: A cooled infusion of dried yarrow aerial parts, applied to the skin with a cotton pad as an astringent toner. Traditionally used for oily and congested skin. Prepare fresh every five days and store in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), Yarrow (Achillea millefolium) entry : astringent properties and skin applications. Traditional western herbal use of yarrow as an external astringent for oily and congested skin.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare fresh every 5 days. Store in a clean glass bottle in the fridge.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keep refrigerated in a clean glass bottle. Use within 5 days. Discard if the liquid becomes cloudy or smells off.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation that temporarily tightens and tones the skin or mucous membranes, traditionally used to reduce oiliness and close pores.

content.text: Yarrow toner is a cooled herbal infusion used externally on the face as an

toner. One teaspoon of dried aerial parts is steeped covered in 200 ml of just-off-boil water for 10 minutes, then strained, cooled, and stored in the fridge. Traditionally applied to oily or congested skin with a cotton pad morning and evening. A fresh batch keeps for five days refrigerated.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

Yarrow is in the Asteraceae (daisy) family. Patch-test this preparation on the inside of your wrist before using it on your face, particularly if you have ever reacted to chamomile, daisies, or ragweed.

In rare cases, yarrow can increase skin sensitivity to sunlight. Do not apply immediately before prolonged direct sun exposure.

Consult a herbalist or your midwife before using this remedy in pregnancy. At the dilution used for a skin toner, external application is generally well tolerated, but yarrow does carry a pregnancy-caution flag and the conservative approach is to check first.

content.text: Bring 200 ml of fresh cold water to the boil, then set aside for one minute.
Place 1 teaspoon of dried yarrow aerial parts in a teapot or covered jug. Pour the just-off-boil water over the herb and cover immediately.
Steep covered for 10 minutes. The water should turn a light straw-yellow.
Strain through a fine sieve into a clean glass bottle or jar. Leave to cool completely, then seal and refrigerate.

Apply a small amount to a cotton pad and sweep over clean, dry skin morning and evening. Leave to dry before applying any moisturiser. Use for up to four weeks, then take a one-week break before a new course.

Keep the toner in a sealed glass bottle in the fridge. Use within five days of making. Discard if the liquid becomes cloudy or develops an off smell. Do not use the same bottle without washing it before making a new batch.
When not to use this remedy
Patch-test before using on your face for the first time. Stop and wash off if any redness, itching, or burning develops.
See a doctor for skin irritation that spreads, weeps, blisters, or comes with fever, and for any rash in someone unwell.
